title: Prior art: open rover boards and finished products

details.roverbase: GPL-3.0 (reference only): 4x18650, regulated supply, power monitoring, 2 brushed motor controllers; its README lists unfinished fixes (connector flip, regulator layout, fuse removal)
details.nasa_jpl_osr: Apache-2.0, 6-wheel rocker-bogie with a Raspberry Pi brain board: proven but far larger and dearer than an indoor inspection rover
details.tinyrover: MIT breakout board for a small rover
details.finished_products: Ring Rover Cam US$999.99 (commercial), SwitchBot K20+ Pro patrol kit ~US$749 plus US$120 hub, Enabot EBO X US$1,025; cheap robot cameras US$20-230 do not climb ramps

title: Strategy: buy proven modules, print the chassis, no custom board
choice: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W + Camera Module 3 for Wi-Fi video, two Pololu DRV8874 carriers (one per side), Pololu 5 V step-down regulator, four Pololu 25D gearmotors on #2676 brackets, printed chassis
because: Every module has a maker datasheet and a price; at one unit a custom board adds fabrication cost and delay for no gain, and the only close open board (roverbase) is GPL and unfinished. Finished patrol robots cost US$750-1,025; cheap robot cameras cannot drive ramps.
alternatives: Custom power + motor board adapted from roverbase (GPL, reference only)
ESP32-CAM board (cheaper, but its specs were not readable from the maker earlier)
2WD with a ball caster (cheaper; chassis tool currently models 4WD)

title: Software: reuse MediaMTX for video, gpiozero for the drivers
choice: MediaMTX (MIT) publishing the Camera Module 3 as WebRTC to a browser; a 70-line Python page with gpiozero PhaseEnableMotor for drive
because: MediaMTX reads Raspberry Pi cameras directly and serves WebRTC to any phone or laptop browser; gpiozero's PhaseEnableMotor matches the DRV8874 phase/enable mode. Nothing to write but glue.
alternatives: rpicam-vid (BSD-2) piping to a custom server

title: hs_project_write_artifact
summary: wrote artifacts/software/rover_drive.py (2026 chars)
claim_boundary: Not run on a Pi or with motors.

inputs.content:
"""HS-ROVER-A drive control: two Pololu DRV8874 carriers in phase/enable mode, driven by gpiozero. Wiring is in wiring.md. Each driver: PMODE to GND (phase/enable), SLEEP to 3.3 V, PH = direction, EN = PWM speed. gpiozero's PhaseEnableMotor drives exactly that interface. Serves a page with drive buttons on port 8000; video comes from MediaMTX (mediamtx.yml) on port 8889. Not yet run on hardware. """ from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer from gpiozero import PhaseEnableMotor LEFT = PhaseEnableMotor(phase=5, enable=12) RIGHT = PhaseEnableMotor(phase=6, enable=13) SPEED = 0.5 # 0.79 m/s at full duty (hs_size_rover_drive), so 0.5 is about 0.4 m/s cruise MOVES = {"forward": (SPEED, SPEED), "back": (-SPEED, -SPEED), "left": (-SPEED, SPEED), "right": (SPEED, -SPEED), "stop": (0, 0)} PAGE = b"""HS-ROVER-A

""" + b"".join(b' " for m in MOVES) + b"

" def apply(move: str) -> None: left, right = MOVES[move] for motor, value in ((LEFT, left), (RIGHT, right)): if value > 0: motor.forward(value) elif value < 0: motor.backward(-value) else: motor.stop() class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler): def do_GET(self): # noqa: N802 move = self.path.strip("/") if move in MOVES: apply(move) self.send_response(204) self.end_headers() return host = (self.headers.get("Host") or "rover.local").split(":")[0].encode() self.send_response(200) self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/html") self.end_headers() self.wfile.write(PAGE.replace(b"%HOST%", host)) if __name__ == "__main__": try: HTTPServer(("0.0.0.0", 8000), Handler).serve_forever() finally: apply("stop")
inputs.claim_boundary: Not run on a Pi or with motors.

title: hs_project_write_artifact
summary: wrote artifacts/wiring.md (1485 chars)
claim_boundary: Wiring not built or powered.

inputs.content:
# HS-ROVER-A wiring

| From | To | Why (source) |
|---|---|---|
| 3S Li-ion pack + (9.0-12.6 V) via 3 A fuse | DRV8874 carrier VIN (both) and D24V22F5 VIN | Driver motor supply 4.5-37 V, reverse-protected on VIN (Pololu #4035); regulator input 5.3-36 V (Pololu #2858) |
| Pack - | All GND | Common ground for logic and motor drivers |
| D24V22F5 VOUT 5 V | Pi Zero 2 W 5 V pin (pin 2) | 5 V 2.5 A regulator (Pololu #2858); bypasses the Pi's input fuse, so the 3 A pack fuse protects the wiring |
| Pi 3.3 V (pin 1) | Both carriers SLEEP | SLEEP needs 1.8-5.5 V to wake the driver (Pololu #4035) |
| GND | Both carriers PMODE | PMODE low before wake = phase/enable mode (Pololu #4035) |
| GPIO5 / GPIO12 | Left carrier PH / EN | Direction / PWM speed (gpiozero PhaseEnableMotor) |
| GPIO6 / GPIO13 | Right carrier PH / EN | Direction / PWM speed |
| Carrier OUT1 / OUT2 | Left and right 25D MP 47:1 motors | One motor per carrier; stall 1.8 A at 12 V is under the carrier's 2.1 A continuous rating (Pololu #3229, #4035) |
| Camera Module 3 | Pi Zero 2 W camera connector | Needs the Zero camera cable (Adafruit 3157), not the module's standard cable |

Logic levels: the Pi's 3.3 V GPIO is inside the DRV8874 carrier's 1.8-5 V logic range (Pololu #4035).
Fuse: 3 A slow-blow at the pack. Both motors stalled draw 3.6 A at 12 V, so a sustained double stall blows it; the
energy budget's normal peak is 0.6 A (hs_energy_budget step 19). Fuse value is a design choice, not a cited rating.

title: Consumer prior art missed: US$30-50 wheeled pet camera (2026-11-26)
build vs buy, revisited
choice: Do not sell HS-ROVER-A as a home or pet camera; keep it only where the cheap robot cannot go
because: the OEM robot costs about one sixth of HS-ROVER-A's US$263 parts and adds night vision, audio, pan/tilt and an app; HS-ROVER-A's only advantages are open local-only video (no vendor cloud), 5 h runtime, 15 degree ramps, 30 mm clearance and full hackability
alternatives: buy the OEM robot as a donor base and replace its firmware or add a Pi (salvage/adapt)
target inspection jobs the toy cannot do (crawlspaces, rough floors, long patrols, privacy-bound sites)
